nodes.title: Hardcoded credential — JWT signing secret
nodes.description: A hardcoded fallback value for the JWT signing secret is present in source code. The value 'jwt-secret-dev-fallback-2024' is used when the ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET environment variable is absent.
nodes.remediationGuidance: Remove the hardcoded fallback. Throw at startup if ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET is absent. Reference from Secrets Manager.

nodes.title: SQL injection via string interpolation in raw query
nodes.description: User-supplied input from query parameter 'q' is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string passed to $queryRawUnsafe in the searchProducts handler.
nodes.snippet: const results = await prisma.$queryRawUnsafe(`...WHERE name ILIKE '%${q}%'...`);
nodes.remediationGuidance: Use prisma.$queryRaw with tagged template literals or Prisma ORM parameterized queries.

nodes.title: Non-constant-time comparison of security token
nodes.description: The resetPassword method compares hashed reset tokens using the !== operator, creating a timing oracle.

nodes.title: User-controlled input used in RegExp constructor
nodes.description: The advancedSearch handler constructs a regular expression from unsanitized user input, enabling ReDoS.
nodes.snippet: const pattern = new RegExp(q as string, "i");
nodes.remediationGuidance: Sanitize input before using in RegExp or switch to database full-text search.

nodes.title: Missing authentication middleware on mutable route
nodes.description: The PUT /reviews/:id route does not include the 'protect' middleware, allowing unauthenticated review modification.
nodes.remediationGuidance: Add protect middleware and verify the authenticated user is the review author.

nodes.title: Path traversal in user-controlled file parameter
nodes.description: The downloadInvoice handler constructs a file path using path.join() with an unsanitized query parameter. An authenticated attacker can supply path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../etc/passwd') to read arbitrary files from the container filesystem.
nodes.remediationGuidance: Validate that the resolved file path starts with the expected base directory. Use path.resolve() and check against the invoicesDir prefix before serving.

nodes.title: Server-side request forgery — unvalidated URL in HTTP client
nodes.description: The verifyOutboundConnectivity handler accepts a URL from the request body and passes it directly to fetch() without validation. An attacker can supply internal addresses (169.254.169.254, VPC-internal endpoints, Redis) to probe the internal network from the server's perspective.
nodes.snippet:
const { url } = req.body;
const response = await fetch(url, { method: "GET", timeout: 5000 });
nodes.remediationGuidance: Validate the supplied URL against an allowlist of permitted external domains. Block private IP ranges and internal hostnames. Consider using a dedicated HTTP proxy with egress controls.

nodes.title: Prototype pollution via bracket notation in Prisma where clause
nodes.description: The filterProducts handler builds a Prisma where clause by iterating over query parameter keys matching the pattern 'where[field]'. The field name is not validated, allowing values like 'where[__proto__][admin]=true' to potentially pollute the object prototype through Prisma's internal processing.

rule.name: Prototype Pollution
rule.owasp: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures

nodes.remediationGuidance: Validate field names against an allowlist of expected property names. Use Object.create(null) for accumulator objects to avoid prototype chain inheritance.

nodes.title: SQL injection via string interpolation in GraphQL resolver
nodes.description: The productSearch GraphQL resolver constructs a PostgreSQL full-text search query using string interpolation of the user-supplied 'query' argument. The interpolation occurs in two locations within the same query string. This endpoint is reached via /api/v1/graphql.
nodes.remediationGuidance: Use parameterized queries. Replace with prisma.$queryRaw tagged template literals.
